text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- The cabinet presented a package of constitutional amendments to Parliament yesterday, drawing the ire of most opposition parties. One amendment would double the number of signatures required to force a referendum to 200,000.

- The Socialist Party's parliamentary group will declare within days that it no longer considers valid a long-standing agreement that no constitutional amendments will be made without the agreement of at least five parliamentary parties.

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn and Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze told a press conference Tuesday that a wide-ranging police operation now underway affects 150 mostly fictitious companies and nearly 200 persons and could be a turning point in the struggle to stamp out organised crime.

- A senior Defence Ministry official said Tuesday that Pentagon officials have pledged military support from NATO, but have also indicated that Hungary's military expenditure should be increased to reach the average of NATO countries, possibly from this year onward.

- The state plans to have 500-600 kilometres of roadway built in the next ten years, to be financed mainly from the Road Fund, Transport Minister Karoly Lotz announced yesterday. The cost of the project is estimated at 312 billion forints, calculated in current prices.
- Domestic industrial production prices increased 1.5 percent between February and March and 21.8 percent since March 1996, the Central Statistics Office reports.
- The international offering of MOL shares closed yesterday five or six times oversubscribed at a price of $16.25 (2,970 forints).
NEPSZABADSAG

- A draft agreement between the Vatican and the government has been completed and will soon be submitted to the cabinet. The agreement seeks to find a lasting solution to finance the public service and activity of the Catholic Church and to settle the state of ecclesiastic properties reclaimed by the Church.
NEPSZAVA
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs announced in Strasbourg Tuesday that Hungary will act as chair of the Council of Europe ministers' committee from autumn 1998 to spring 1999.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The industry will increase its role in the following few years, to make up 28 percent of Hungary's GDP, a top Industry and Trade ministry official told a conference in Gyor on Tuesday.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- Industry, Trade and Tourism Minister Szabolcs Fazakas told a conference in New York that the central bank planned to reduce the forint devaluation rate below one percent from 1.1 percent in the second half of 1997 but National Bank of Hungary (NBH) president Gyorgy Suranyi denied that the NBH's devaluation policy changed.

- The State Money and Capital Market Supervision refused to issue a banking license to a group including former Finance Minister and Budapest Bank chief Lajos Bokros and Szabolcs Szekeres, former president of the State Holding Co.
NAPI GAZDASAG

- Foreign investors have subscribed 1.428 million Zalakeramia shares in the international offering which closed Tuesday in London. The shares fetched a price of $35.86 or 7,000 forints, some 12 percent less than the Budapest Stock Exchange price.
-- Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327 4040
